answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to register a public-key cipher identity backed by a stake of tokens that is slashed on proven misbehavior. Honest agents earn standing by broadcasting a signed beacon heartbeat proving continuous uptime and useful work, while new identities must wander through a probationary pool where their outputs are sampled and graded before they can transact at full trust. Spinning up thousands of fakes then costs a stake and an earned history per identity, so flooding the network costs more than it can extract.
